heatmap.title: Heatmaps of {label}, one per plate: read {number} of {total} ({time})

meaning.raw: Raw data: the values as they were imported from the measurement files (or made with the measurement calculator of the experiment). The colour shows how much signal a well gave; a well without colour has no value.
meaning.log10: log10(1 + value) of {source}, calculated on the plate page: one more means about 10 times more signal, one less about 10 times less.
meaning.correction: {source} minus the {method} of the {reference} wells of the same plate (background correction on the plate page): 0 = as much signal as the background, below 0 = less. The {reference} wells stay empty.
meaning.inhibition: %Inhibition of {source} between the controls of each plate (normalization on the plate page): 0 = like {negative} (no effect), 1 = like {positive} (full effect).
meaning.activity: %Activity of {source} between the controls of each plate (normalization on the plate page), in percent: 100 = like {negative} (the signal without the effect), 0 = like {positive} (full effect).

heatmap.open_plate: Click a plate to open its page: there the formula is shown with the numbers of that plate.
heatmap.missing_plates: {count} of {total} plates do not have this measurement (it was not imported or not calculated for them), so their heatmaps stay empty.
heatmap.scale_shared: All plates use one colour scale (the values of all plates together), so the same colour means the same value on every plate and the plates can be compared.
heatmap.scale_per_plate: "Per plate view": every plate has its own colour scale from its own values (see the legend next to it), so the same colour can mean different values on different plates; compare the patterns within a plate, not the colours between plates.

stats.explanation: z' and SSMD show how clearly the positive ({positive}) and the negative ({negative}) control wells are apart at this time point, that is how good the test on the plate is. Both use the median and the MAD (the typical spread around the median) of each control; the controls are the ones chosen in "Positive control" and "Negative control".
stats.reading: z' above 0.5 = a good test (the controls are clearly apart), 0 to 0.5 = usable, below 0 = the controls overlap. SSMD: how many typical spreads lie between the two medians; the larger, the better.

background_correction.formula: corrected value = (value of the well in {source}) - {method}(values of the {reference} wells)
background_correction.reading: 0 = as much signal as the background (the {method} of the {reference} wells), above 0 = more signal, below 0 = less. The {reference} wells stay empty. Calculated separately for each time point.
background_correction.reading_log10: {source} is in log10 values, and subtracting log10 values means dividing: 0 = as much signal as the background (the {method} of the {reference} wells), 0.3 = 2 times as much, 1 = 10 times as much, -0.3 = half of it, -1 = a tenth. The {reference} wells stay empty. Calculated separately for each time point.

calculations.main_is_calculated: The heatmap above shows {label}, calculated on this page: how it was calculated is explained with its own heatmap below.
calculations.none_calculated: Nothing is calculated on this plate yet. With "Add calculation" you can calculate new values, e.g. a background correction; each one gets its own heatmap here.

calculations.title: Add calculation

descriptions.background_correction: The median or mean of the reference wells is subtracted from every other well of this plate, at each time point. The result is saved as a new measurement of the plate; the reference wells stay empty.
descriptions.log10: log10(1 + value) of every well is saved as a new measurement of the plate, e.g. Lum1_log10; with the 1, a well with 0 still gets a value (log10(1) = 0). A well with a value of -1 or below is left empty.
descriptions.normalization: Every well is normalized between the negative and the positive control on the log10(1 + value) scale. Two new measurements are saved: the %Inhibition (negative control 0, positive control 1) and the %Activity = (1 - %Inhibition) × 100 (negative control 100, positive control 0). Use the raw readout, e.g. Lum1, not background-corrected values: their values below 0 compress the scale, and wells of -1 or below have no log10 and are left out, controls too.

calculations.negative_control: Negative control (no effect, e.g. only the solvent DMSO)
calculations.positive_control: Positive control (full effect, e.g. a known reference compound)
calculations.read_caption: Numbers of read {number} of {total} ({time}), the time point chosen in "Select timestamp".

raw.title: Raw data: {label}
raw.description: The values as they were imported from the measurement file (or made with the measurement calculator of the experiment); nothing is calculated from them here. Every square of the heatmap is one well.
raw.description_imported: Imported from the file {file}: the values as they are in the file; nothing is calculated from them on this page. A file can also hold values the software of the instrument already calculated (e.g. a name like Lum1_corrected); how, the file does not say. Every square of the heatmap is one well.
raw.description_calculator: Made with the measurement calculator of the experiment ("Add Measurement"), not imported from a file and not calculated on this page. The calculator does not save its formula, so it cannot be shown here. Every square of the heatmap is one well.
raw.reading: the colour shows how much signal a well gave: the legend next to the heatmap runs from the lowest value (bottom) to the highest (top). A well without colour has no value. Below: the median of every well type (the middle value: half of the wells are above it, half below). The median of the reference wells (R, N1 or NREF) is the background, the signal the test gives on its own; "Add calculation" → Background correction subtracts it from the other wells.

log10.title: log10: {label}
log10.formula: log10 value = log10(1 + value of the well in {source})
log10.reading: one more means about 10 times more signal, one less about 10 times less (3 → 999, 2 → 99).
log10.skipped: {count} well(s) left empty: a value of -1 or below has no log10(1 + value).

normalization.inhibition_formula: %Inhibition = (log10(1 + value of the well) - median(log10(1 + value) of the {negative} wells)) / (median(log10(1 + value) of the {positive} wells) - median(log10(1 + value) of the {negative} wells))
normalization.inhibition_reading: 0 = like {negative} (no effect), 1 = like {positive} (full effect), 0.5 = half of the full effect. Below 0 or above 1 = beyond the controls. Fractions: 0.5 means 50 %. Calculated separately for each time point; a well with a value of -1 or below stays empty. The colours of the heatmap run from the lowest to the highest value of this plate (see the legend), not fixed from 0 to 1.
normalization.activity_reading: 100 = like {negative} (the signal without the effect), 0 = like {positive} (full effect), 50 = half of the full effect. Below 0 or above 100 = beyond the controls. In percent. Calculated separately for each time point; a well with a value of -1 or below stays empty. The colours of the heatmap run from the lowest to the highest value of this plate (see the legend), not fixed from 0 to 100.
normalization.skipped_controls: Among them {negativeCount} {negative} and {positiveCount} {positive} control well(s): the medians of the controls are taken without them, so the two ends of the scale (the values of the controls) can be off. Normalize the raw readout (not background-corrected values) to keep all controls.
normalization.controls_overlap: The {negative} and {positive} controls are not clearly apart (z' = {zPrime} on these values): the spread of their wells is larger than the distance between their medians, so these values are not reliable. Check that the right well types are chosen as the controls.

scale_note.full: Colours: from the lowest value ({min}) at one end of the palette to the highest ({max}) at the other; every well gets the colour of where its value lies between them. A few extreme wells can take most of the scale; then choose the robust colour scale.
scale_note.robust: Colours (robust): from {min} to {max} = the median ± 3 MAD (the typical spread around the median), so that a few extreme wells do not take all the colours. Wells beyond these ends get the end colour (≥ / ≤ in the legend).

empty_wells.title: Empty Wells
empty_wells.paragraph_1: Here you can see plates with problematic wells (wells with amount or DMSO concentration below the threshold). This information is also shown in the navigation tree as warning indicators. You can change the threshold here and recalculate well and plate status.
empty_wells.paragraph_2: This information comes from Echo transfer files: wells are marked when a transfer file is imported. After changing the thresholds, or to update older plates, use "Recalculate based on current threshold" - it checks all library plates again. Please do not import a transfer file a second time, because the withdrawn volumes would then be counted twice.
